requirements.title: Computing literacy
requirements.summary: Complete at least 3 credits in introductory computational thinking; consult the linked approved list. The degree plan specifies its own computing courses.

requirements.title: History and humanities progression
requirements.summary: At least 18 credits: ENGL 101 and 102 (6), 200-level history/humanities (3), 300-level history/humanities (6), and HSS senior seminar (3). These describe the plan’s GER allocations, not additional requirements to sum again.

requirements.title: Quantitative reasoning
requirements.summary: At least 6 introductory quantitative-reasoning credits, including probability/statistics content in one course; degree-specific mathematics/statistics courses remain in the plan.

requirements.title: Scientific literacy laboratory condition
requirements.summary: At least 7 natural-science credits including laboratory experience. The plan divides these into 3-credit and 4-credit slots; the source does not provide a blanket lecture/lab pairing rule.

requirements.title: Social science literacy
requirements.summary: At least 3 credits in appropriate social science or management-related study; consult the approved list and degree-specific courses.

requirements.title: First-year seminar
requirements.summary: First-time full-time freshmen must attend first-year seminar; the plan lists FYS SEM at zero credits.

requirements.title: GER minima and degree-specific requirements
requirements.summary: GERs are university minima. College and department requirements may exceed them; neither an eligible pool nor a minimum certifies permission to reuse one course in multiple degree slots.

requirements.title: Graduation and major GPA
requirements.summary: Complete the curriculum, attain a cumulative 2.0 GPA in its required courses and a 2.0 GPA in department-defined upper-division major requirements, and submit the graduation application by the university deadline.

requirements.title: Transfer-student upper-division residency
requirements.summary: Transfer students must complete at NJIT at least 33 upper-division credits approved by their major department.

requirements.title: Transfer equivalence and grades
requirements.summary: Transfer credit requires course equivalence, a minimum C grade and official transcript documentation. There is no general transfer-credit cap, but the NJIT upper-division residency requirement applies. Foreign coursework needs the stated evaluation and descriptions.

requirements.title: Courses taken at another institution
requirements.summary: Outside the cross-registration program, obtain prior department approval and the registrar/home-department signatures, then provide an official transcript with C or higher. At most two humanities/social-science GER equivalents may be taken elsewhere during summers; the HSS capstone must be at NJIT. Summer Rutgers-Newark/Essex courses are permitted only when unavailable at NJIT. Summer calculus I/II courses elsewhere must span at least eight weeks and physics I/II at least six.

requirements.title: Course repetition limit
requirements.summary: A course may be attempted at most four times across NJIT and other institutions, including withdrawals. Four unsuccessful attempts at a required course make the student ineligible for programs requiring it. Repeating excludes only the lowest grade from the cumulative GPA; other grades remain. Forgoing incoming transfer credit is irreversible.

requirements.title: Expiration of earned credits
requirements.summary: NJIT course credits normally expire after ten years and must be replaced unless the offering/approving department grants an extension. External coursework older than ten years requires departmental applicability review; transfer-credit procedures depend on associate-degree status.

requirements.title: Unsatisfactory work earns no degree credit
requirements.summary: U grades do not earn degree credit. S/U reports progress in the specified co-op, teaching methods, ESL and physical education courses; this is not a general elective pass/fail permission.

requirements.title: PHYS 103A laboratory relationship
requirements.summary: Conditional when selecting this GER option; not an additional required course group. Take PHYS 103 concurrently with PHYS 103A; its separately stated prerequisite sequence and grade condition also apply.

requirements.title: PHYS 111A laboratory relationship
requirements.summary: Conditional when selecting this GER option; not an additional required course group. Take PHYS 111 concurrently with PHYS 111A; the lecture also names MATH 111 as a corequisite.

requirements.title: PHYS 121A laboratory relationship
requirements.summary: Conditional when selecting this GER option; not an additional required course group. PHYS 121A requires concurrent PHYS 121 or PHYS 122 and its stated prerequisites. PHYS 121 is in the reviewed GER pool; this course-description alternative does not add PHYS 122 to that pool.

requirements.title: PHYS 202A laboratory relationship
requirements.summary: Conditional when selecting this GER option; not an additional required course group. PHYS 202A is an optional lab associated with PHYS 202. The description does not state a concurrent-enrollment requirement; none is invented.

requirements.title: PHYS 203A laboratory relationship
requirements.summary: Conditional when selecting this GER option; not an additional required course group. The optional PHYS 203A laboratory has PHYS 203 as a corequisite.

requirements.title: CHEM 125A laboratory relationship
requirements.summary: Conditional when selecting this GER option; not an additional required course group. CHEM 125A permits either CHEM 125 or CHEM 121 as its corequisite lecture, not both.

requirements.title: CHEM 126A laboratory relationship
requirements.summary: Conditional when selecting this GER option; not an additional required course group. CHEM 126A requires CHEM 125A with C or better and either CHEM 126 or CHEM 122 concurrently.

requirements.title: BIOL 150 laboratory relationship
requirements.summary: Conditional when selecting this GER option; not an additional required course group. BIOL 150 is explicitly described as a laboratory course, with lecture and laboratory contact hours in its catalog heading.
